title: introduce-adaptive-lint-adapters-and-slimline-test-orchestrator
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduces adaptive lint adapters and a lightweight test orchestrator; no user-facing API changes. Improves PR feedback latency and reduces CI cost for small changes.
description:
Motivation: Our monorepo runs a single heavy lint+test pipeline which creates long feedback loops and high CI costs on trivial changes. This PR splits the lint/test responsibilities into small, language-aware adapters and introduces a slimline test orchestrator that selects and runs only what is required for a change.

Summary: Implement an adapter interface for language/tool-specific lint runners, add Python/TypeScript/Go adapters, replace monolithic presubmit job with a staged presubmit that runs fast-path checks first (fast-lint, unit-smoke) and defers heavier integration suites to a gated lane. Switch CI runner image to a containerd-based build image (smaller, faster startup), and remove legacy bash wrapper scripts in favor of Go-based entrypoints in tools/ci. Also bump GitHub Action versions and pin a few vulnerable dev-deps.

Key changes: - Add tools/ci/adapter/iface.go and per-language adapters (tools/ci/adapter/python_adapter.go, ts_adapter.go, go_adapter.go) - Introduce tools/ci/orchestrator/*: lightweight scheduler that computes minimal job set based on changed paths and adapter metadata - Replace .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml with staged-presubmit.yml that wires fast lanes and gated heavy lanes - New container image docker/ci/runner: Dockerfile + smaller runtime, based on distroless + containerd - Remove scripts/run-lint.sh and scripts/run-tests.sh (deprecated) - Update README/CONTRIBUTING with new presubmit guidance and debug instructions

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2101) + implementation plan - [x] Unit tests for adapters and orchestrator decision logic - [x] E2E smoke on ephemeral runner - [x] Rollout plan and feature-flag gating - [x] Rollback instructions included in runbook

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover adapter selection and mapping from changed files to job graph. Ran a staged rollout behind a feature flag for 48 hours on the infra CI and verified median PR feedback decreased from ~9m to ~2m for small doc/TS fixes. Integration suites were deferred and run in a gated lane; on average we observed a 22% CI minute reduction across the org during the canary.

Compatibility and migration: Existing presubmit behavior is preserved behind a feature flag. Ops can enable the staged presubmit via the repo-level config (tools/ci/config.yaml). The old bash scripts are retained in the release branch for a 2-week grace period but deprecated.

Risks and mitigations: - Adapter bugs could miss required checks: we added conservative fallback to run monolithic pipeline if orchestrator faces an error. - Runner image changes may surface subtle environment differences: included host-compat smoke tests and a one-week canary.

Rollout plan: Merge to main under feature flag OFF. Enable on the infra CI for canary -> enable for org members -> enable org-wide after 7 days and monitoring.

Related: builds on prior CI hygiene work (ENG-1724) and incorporates learnings from recent flaky-test runbook (SUP-1284).
